perspectives.label: The Individual Gambler
perspectives.comment: The individual gambler, even if unaware of the theorem, is ultimately subject to its statistical inevitability.

perspectives.label: The House (Casino)
perspectives.comment: The house benefits from the theorem's consequences, understanding the statistical advantage over time.

perspectives.label: The Analytical Observer
perspectives.comment: An objective observer recognizes Gambler's Ruin as a mathematical certainty within the specified conditions.

commentary.narrative_context: Gambler's Ruin is a statistical theorem stating that a gambler with finite wealth, playing a fair or negative-expectation game against an opponent with effectively infinite wealth (the "House"), will eventually go bankrupt with a probability approaching 1. This is a mathematical inevitability.
commentary.logic_rationale: Extractiveness is low as the theorem describes a probabilistic outcome rather than a direct extraction. Suppression is also low as the gambler is free to choose whether or not to gamble. Theater ratio is zero as there is no performative aspect to the theorem. The theorem emerges naturally from the mathematics of probability.
commentary.perspectival_gap: All agents, from the powerless gambler to the powerful house and the analytical observer, ultimately perceive the theorem as a mathematical certainty, leading to a Mountain classification from all perspectives.
commentary.directionality_logic: While the House benefits from the theorem in the long run, the theorem itself isn't an active extraction mechanism. It's a probabilistic description of outcomes. Therefore, the perspective is largely the same from different agents.
